Underscore-prefixed so build.sh never auto-imports it; test_kinds.py does.

passages.title: Down the Rabbit-Hole
passages.source_note: Public domain: the opening of 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland' by Lewis Carroll (1865), Chapter I.
passages.text:
Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it.

So she was considering in her own mind whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her.

There was nothing so very remarkable in that; nor did Alice think it so very much out of the way to hear the Rabbit say to itself that it would be late. But when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet, for it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket or a watch to take out of it.

questions.stem: What did Alice complain that her sister's book lacked?
questions.explanation: Alice thinks a book is no use without pictures or conversations.

questions.stem: Why does Alice jump to her feet?

options.text: Because a rabbit with a waistcoat-pocket and a watch is like nothing she has seen
Because she has finished her daisy-chain
Because the rabbit speaks to her directly

questions.explanation: A talking rabbit did not surprise her; the watch and waistcoat-pocket did.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'remarkable' as it is used in the passage.
questions.explanation: The narrator means there was nothing out of the ordinary in it.

questions.stem: Which word best replaces 'hurried' without changing the meaning?
questions.explanation: The Rabbit is in a hurry, so 'rushed' keeps the sense.
